migration_guide: Step 1: Dependencies - All required dependencies (springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui v2.3.0) have been added to pom.xml for all three services
Step 2: Configuration - OpenApiConfiguration.java classes created for each service with @OpenAPIDefinition and @SecurityScheme annotations
Step 3: Application Properties - Add springdoc configuration to application.yml for each service (see SWAGGER_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md)
Step 4: Controller Annotations - All controllers updated with @Tag, @Operation, @ApiResponses, @Parameter, and @SecurityRequirement annotations
Step 5: Build Project - Run 'mvn clean install' for each service to compile with new dependencies
Step 6: Start Services - Start all three microservices (User Management on 8081, Product Catalog on 8082, Shopping Cart on 8083)

Step 7: Access Swagger UI - Navigate to http://localhost:8081/swagger-ui.html (User Management), http://localhost:8082/swagger-ui.html (Product Catalog), http://localhost:8083/swagger-ui.html (Shopping Cart)
Step 8: Test Authentication - Use POST /api/v1/users/login to obtain JWT token, then click 'Authorize' button in Swagger UI and enter 'Bearer <token>'
Step 9: Test Endpoints - Use Swagger UI to test all documented endpoints with 'Try it out' feature
Step 10: OpenAPI Specification - Access OpenAPI JSON at http://localhost:8081/api-docs (and 8082, 8083 for other services)
Step 11: Security Configuration - Ensure Spring Security configuration permits access to /swagger-ui/**, /api-docs/**, and /v3/api-docs/** paths
Step 12: Production Deployment - For production, consider disabling Swagger UI by setting springdoc.swagger-ui.enabled=false in application-prod.yml
Step 13: API Gateway Integration - If using API Gateway, configure routes to expose Swagger UI from all services
Step 14: Documentation Review - Review generated documentation for accuracy and completeness
Step 15: Team Training - Share SWAGGER_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md with development team for reference
